_doc:
G0 — zero-LLM template feedback for DT taxonomy v6 (Track D, 2026-11-14).

Hand-written for this experiment (AI-drafted, NOT native-reviewed). Three per-error
styles + an item summary, keyed by v6 subtype slug and learner L1:

  direct  "X -> Y" with the type label              (needs learner_form, corrected_form)
  meta    the rule, <=25 words, never gives the answer (needs learner_form only)
  hint    elicitation question, never gives the answer (needs learner_form only)
  summary 1-2 sentences, item level                 (needs error list + severities)

Placeholders: {l} learner_form, {c} corrected_form, {label} type label.
L1 coverage: `en` for every v6 slug (40); `zh` and `ja` for the 20 slugs of the
English-L2 list (the only L2 whose learners got a zh/ja L1 in this experiment).
Run `python g0_templates.py` to dump templates.json.

en.clean: Your version says everything the original says — nothing needs fixing. Where your wording differs from the reference, it is an acceptable alternative.
en.one: Almost all of your version matches the original. One thing to fix: {label} at “{l}”.
en.many: Most of your version matches the original and the message comes through. Fix this first: {label} at “{l}”.
en.critical: Most of the passage is accurate, but one spot changes the meaning. Fix this first: {label} at “{l}”.

zh.clean: 你的译文把原文的意思都表达出来了，没有需要修改的地方。和参考译文措辞不同之处，都是可以接受的说法。
zh.one: 你的译文几乎全部与原文一致。需要修改一处：“{l}”这里的{label}问题。
zh.many: 你的译文大部分与原文一致，意思也传达到了。最先要改的是：“{l}”这里的{label}问题。
zh.critical: 译文大部分是准确的，但有一处改变了原意。最先要改的是：“{l}”这里的{label}问题。

ja.clean: 原文の内容がすべて表現できています。直すところはありません。参照文と言い方が違う部分も、問題のない言い換えです。
ja.one: ほぼ全体が原文と一致しています。直すのは一か所：「{l}」の{label}です。
ja.many: 大部分が原文と一致していて、内容は伝わります。まず直したいのは「{l}」の{label}です。
ja.critical: 大部分は正確ですが、一か所で意味が変わっています。まず直したいのは「{l}」の{label}です。

en.label: Missing element
en.meta: Every piece of meaning in the original must appear in your version. Around “{l}”, something the original says has no counterpart.
en.hint: Compare “{l}” with the meaning you were asked to express: which idea has gone missing?

zh.label: 成分缺失
zh.meta: 原文的每一层意思都要译出来。“{l}”这里少了原文中的一个成分。
zh.hint: 把“{l}”和要表达的意思对照一下：少了哪一层意思？

ja.label: 要素の欠落
ja.meta: 原文の内容はすべて訳文に入れる必要があります。「{l}」のあたりで、原文にある要素が一つ抜けています。
ja.hint: 「{l}」を、表したい意味と比べてみましょう。どの内容が抜けていますか。

en.label: Added element
en.meta: Don't add information the original doesn't contain. Part of “{l}” says something the source never said.
en.hint: Which word(s) in “{l}” have no counterpart in the meaning you were given?

zh.label: 多余成分
zh.meta: 不要添加原文没有的内容。“{l}”里有原文没说的东西。
zh.hint: “{l}”里哪个词在原文的意思中找不到对应？

ja.label: 余分な要素
ja.meta: 原文にない情報を足してはいけません。「{l}」には原文にない内容が含まれています。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の中で、原文の意味に対応しない語はどれですか。

en.label: Word choice
en.meta: A word here doesn't carry the meaning the passage needs. Words that look alike or share a translation often differ in meaning or use.
en.hint: Does “{l}” mean exactly what the original says? Which word in it means something different?

zh.label: 用词不当
zh.meta: 这里有一个词表达不出原文需要的意思。看起来相近或中文译法相同的词，意思和用法往往不同。
zh.hint: “{l}”的意思和原文完全一样吗？其中哪个词的意思不对？

ja.label: 語彙選択
ja.meta: ここで使った語は、文が必要とする意味を表していません。形や訳語が似ていても、意味や使い方が違う語があります。
ja.hint: 「{l}」は原文と同じ意味になっていますか。意味がずれている語はどれでしょう。

en.label: Collocation
en.meta: Some words habitually go together. The combination in “{l}” is understandable, but it is not the pairing native speakers use.
en.hint: Which word normally partners with the other words in “{l}”? Try recalling the phrase as one fixed chunk.

zh.label: 搭配不当
zh.meta: 有些词习惯上固定搭配。“{l}”能看懂，但不是母语者惯用的搭配。
zh.hint: “{l}”里的词通常和哪个词搭配？试着把它当作一个固定短语来回想。

ja.label: コロケーション
ja.meta: 語には決まった組み合わせがあります。「{l}」は意味は通じますが、母語話者が使う組み合わせではありません。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の語は、ふつうどの語と一緒に使われますか。決まり文句として思い出してみましょう。

en.label: Word order
en.meta: The words are right but their order is not. This language fixes where this kind of element sits in the sentence.
en.hint: All the words in “{l}” are fine — can you rearrange them into the order this language requires?

zh.label: 语序错误
zh.meta: 用的词没错，但顺序不对。这种成分在句中的位置是固定的。
zh.hint: “{l}”里的词都对——你能把它们排成正确的顺序吗？

ja.label: 語順
ja.meta: 使った語は正しいですが、順番が違います。この種の要素は文中の位置が決まっています。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の語はすべて合っています。正しい順番に並べ替えられますか。

en.label: Register
en.meta: Formality should match the rest of the passage. “{l}” is noticeably more casual or more formal than the text around it.
en.hint: Read “{l}” next to the sentences around it: does the level of formality match? How would it sound in the passage's style?

zh.label: 语体不符
zh.meta: 正式程度要和全文一致。“{l}”比上下文明显更随意或更正式。
zh.hint: 把“{l}”和前后句子放在一起读：语气一致吗？用文章的风格该怎么说？

ja.label: 文体・レジスター
ja.meta: 改まり度は文章全体でそろえます。「{l}」は前後の文より明らかにくだけている、または硬すぎます。
ja.hint: 「{l}」を前後の文と並べて読んでみましょう。文体は合っていますか。文章の調子に合わせるとどうなりますか。

en.label: Spelling / script
en.meta: The word is the right one but it is written incorrectly.
en.hint: Look closely at how “{l}” is written — can you spot the spelling or character slip?

zh.label: 拼写错误
zh.meta: 词选对了，但写法有误。
zh.hint: 仔细看看“{l}”的写法——能发现拼写上的问题吗？

ja.label: 表記
ja.meta: 語は合っていますが、書き方が間違っています。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の書き方をよく見てください。つづりの間違いに気づけますか。

en.label: Linking word
en.meta: Linking words signal how ideas relate (contrast, cause, sequence). The link here signals a different relationship from the original's.
en.hint: How are the two ideas around “{l}” related — contrast, cause, sequence? Which linking word signals that?

zh.label: 衔接词
zh.meta: 连接词表示前后内容的关系（转折、因果、顺序）。这里用的连接词表示的关系和原文不同。
zh.hint: “{l}”前后两层意思是什么关系——转折、因果还是顺序？哪个连接词能表示这种关系？

ja.label: つなぎの言葉
ja.meta: 接続表現は前後の関係（逆接・因果・順序）を示します。ここで使った表現は、原文とは違う関係を示しています。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の前後の内容はどんな関係ですか（逆接・因果・順序）。それを示すつなぎの言葉は何でしょう。

en.label: Doesn't make sense
en.meta: The sentence is grammatical, but the words combine into something that does not make sense in the real world.
en.hint: Read “{l}” literally: can that actually happen? Which word makes it strange?

zh.label: 语义不通
zh.meta: 句子语法没错，但词语组合起来在现实中说不通。
zh.hint: 按字面读“{l}”：这真的可能吗？是哪个词让它变得奇怪？

ja.label: 意味が通らない
ja.meta: 文法は合っていますが、語の組み合わせが現実にはあり得ない内容になっています。
ja.hint: 「{l}」を文字どおりに読んでみましょう。実際にあり得ますか。おかしくしているのはどの語ですか。

en.label: Contradiction
en.meta: This part states something that conflicts with another part of your own text or with the original.
en.hint: Does “{l}” agree with what the rest of the passage says? Where is the clash?

zh.label: 前后矛盾
zh.meta: 这一处和你译文的其他部分或原文相矛盾。
zh.hint: “{l}”和文章其他地方说的一致吗？矛盾在哪里？

ja.label: 矛盾
ja.meta: この部分は、あなたの文章の他の部分、または原文と食い違っています。
ja.hint: 「{l}」は文章の他の部分と合っていますか。どこが食い違っていますか。

en.label: Meaning reversed
en.meta: Your wording says the opposite of the original — usually a lost or added negative, or an opposite word. This changes the whole message.
en.hint: Compare what “{l}” says with the original meaning: is one positive and the other negative? What flips it?

zh.label: 意思相反
zh.meta: 你的说法和原文意思相反——通常是漏掉或多加了否定词，或用了反义词。这会改变整句话的意思。
zh.hint: 把“{l}”和原文的意思比一比：是不是一个肯定、一个否定？是什么让意思反过来了？

ja.label: 意味の反転
ja.meta: 原文と反対の意味になっています。否定語の抜け・付け足しや、反対語の使用が主な原因です。文全体の内容が変わってしまいます。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の意味を原文と比べてみましょう。肯定と否定が逆になっていませんか。何が意味を逆にしていますか。

en.label: Article / determiner
en.meta: A singular countable noun needs a determiner (a/an, the, this…). Which one depends on whether the reader already knows the thing.
en.hint: Look at the noun in “{l}”: is it singular and countable? Is it mentioned for the first time? What small word does it need?

zh.label: 冠词/限定词
zh.meta: 英语的可数名词单数前必须有限定词（a/an、the、this等）；用哪个取决于读者是否已经知道所指的事物。
zh.hint: 看“{l}”里的名词：是可数名词单数吗？是第一次提到吗？它前面需要哪个小词？

ja.label: 冠詞・限定詞
ja.meta: 英語の数えられる名詞の単数形には限定詞（a/an, the, this など）が必要です。どれを使うかは、読み手がその物をすでに知っているかで決まります。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の名詞を見てください。数えられる名詞の単数形ですか。初めて出てくる物ですか。前にどんな短い語が必要でしょう。

en.label: Preposition
en.meta: Prepositions are fixed by the verb, noun or meaning they attach to; they rarely translate one-to-one from your language.
en.hint: Which preposition does the verb or noun in “{l}” normally take for this meaning?

zh.label: 介词
zh.meta: 英语介词由它搭配的动词、名词或要表达的意思决定，很少能和中文一一对应。
zh.hint: “{l}”里的动词或名词，表达这个意思时通常搭配哪个介词？

ja.label: 前置詞
ja.meta: 英語の前置詞は、結びつく動詞・名詞や表す意味によって決まり、日本語の助詞と一対一には対応しません。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の動詞や名詞は、この意味のときふつうどの前置詞をとりますか。

en.label: Verb form / tense
en.meta: The verb's form must match the time of the passage and whatever the nearby verbs require.
en.hint: When does the action in “{l}” happen, compared with the rest of the passage? Which verb form shows that?

zh.label: 动词形式/时态
zh.meta: 动词的形式要和文章的时间一致，也要符合前后动词的要求。
zh.hint: 和文章其他部分相比，“{l}”里的动作发生在什么时候？哪种动词形式能表示这个时间？

ja.label: 動詞の形・時制
ja.meta: 動詞の形は、文章全体の時間や前後の動詞が求める形に合わせます。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の動作は、文章の他の部分と比べていつのことですか。それを表す動詞の形は何でしょう。

en.label: Verb pattern
en.meta: Each verb dictates the pattern after it: to + verb, -ing, a that-clause or an object. The pattern used here doesn't fit this verb.
en.hint: What form must follow the main verb in “{l}” — to + verb, -ing, or a clause?

zh.label: 动词句型
zh.meta: 每个动词后面接什么形式是固定的：to do、doing、that从句或宾语。这里的形式和这个动词不搭配。
zh.hint: “{l}”里的主要动词后面应该接什么形式——to do、doing，还是从句？

ja.label: 動詞の文型
ja.meta: 動詞ごとに後ろに続く形（to不定詞、-ing、that節、目的語）が決まっています。ここの形はこの動詞に合いません。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の動詞の後ろには、to不定詞・-ing・節のどれが続きますか。

en.label: Agreement
en.meta: A verb must agree with its subject in number and person, and words like this/these must agree with their noun.
en.hint: Find the subject (or noun) in “{l}”: is it singular or plural? Does the word that goes with it match?

zh.label: 一致关系
zh.meta: 动词要和主语在人称和单复数上保持一致；this/these这类词也要和后面的名词一致。
zh.hint: 找出“{l}”里的主语（或名词）：是单数还是复数？和它搭配的词一致吗？

ja.label: 一致
ja.meta: 動詞は主語の数・人称に一致させます。this/these のような語も後ろの名詞に一致させます。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の主語（または名詞）は単数ですか、複数ですか。それと組む語の形は合っていますか。

en.label: Pronoun
en.meta: A pronoun must match what it refers to in number, person and gender, and take the right case (it/its, they/them/their).
en.hint: What exactly does the pronoun in “{l}” refer back to? Is that one thing or several?

zh.label: 代词
zh.meta: 代词要和它所指的对象在单复数、人称、性别上一致，并用正确的格（it/its、they/them/their）。
zh.hint: “{l}”里的代词指的到底是什么？是一个还是多个？

ja.label: 代名詞
ja.meta: 代名詞は、指すものの数・人称・性に合わせ、正しい格（it/its, they/them/their）を使います。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の代名詞は何を指していますか。それは一つですか、複数ですか。

en.label: Singular / plural
en.meta: Countable nouns show number: a plural ending for more than one. Uncountable nouns take no plural.
en.hint: How many things are meant in “{l}” — one or more? Does the noun's form show that?

zh.label: 单复数
zh.meta: 可数名词要体现数量：不止一个时要用复数形式；不可数名词没有复数。
zh.hint: “{l}”里指的是一个还是多个？名词的形式体现出来了吗？

ja.label: 単数・複数
ja.meta: 数えられる名詞は数を形で表します。二つ以上なら複数形にし、数えられない名詞は複数形にしません。
ja.hint: 「{l}」が指すものは一つですか、二つ以上ですか。名詞の形はそれを表していますか。

en.label: Phrasal verb
en.meta: A phrasal verb is a verb plus one specific particle; a different particle changes the meaning or breaks the expression.
en.hint: The verb in “{l}” is fine — which small word (up, out, on, off…) completes it for this meaning?

zh.label: 短语动词
zh.meta: 短语动词是“动词+固定的小品词”；换一个小品词，意思就变了或不成立。
zh.hint: “{l}”里的动词没错——表达这个意思时，后面该接哪个小词（up、out、on、off等）？

ja.label: 句動詞
ja.meta: 句動詞は「動詞＋決まった小辞」の組み合わせです。小辞が変わると意味が変わるか、表現として成り立ちません。
ja.hint: 「{l}」の動詞は合っています。この意味にするには、後ろにどの短い語（up, out, on, off など）が必要ですか。

en.label: Word form
en.meta: Right word family, wrong member: this slot in the sentence needs a different part of speech (noun, verb, adjective, adverb).
en.hint: What part of speech does the slot in “{l}” need — noun, verb, adjective or adverb? Which form of the word is that?

zh.label: 词形/词性
zh.meta: 词族选对了，但词性不对：句中这个位置需要另一种词性（名词、动词、形容词或副词）。
zh.hint: “{l}”里这个位置需要什么词性——名词、动词、形容词还是副词？这个词对应的形式是什么？

ja.label: 語形・品詞
ja.meta: 語のグループは合っていますが品詞が違います。文のこの位置には別の品詞（名詞・動詞・形容詞・副詞）が必要です。
ja.hint: 「{l}」のこの位置にはどの品詞が必要ですか。その語のどの形がそれに当たりますか。

en.label: Measure word
en.meta: After a number or 这/那, each Chinese noun takes its own measure word; 个 cannot stand in for all of them.
en.hint: What kind of thing is the noun in “{l}”? Which measure word goes with that kind of noun?

en.label: Aspect / negation
en.meta: 了, 过 and 着 mark completed, experienced and ongoing actions; 不 negates habits and the future, 没 negates what did not happen.
en.hint: In “{l}”, is the action completed, experienced, ongoing or habitual? Which marker (or which negator) expresses that?

en.label: 的 / 地 / 得
en.meta: 的 links a modifier to a noun, 地 links a manner word to a verb, and 得 introduces a complement after a verb.
en.hint: In “{l}”, what follows the de — a noun, a verb, or a description of how the action turned out?

en.label: Complement
en.meta: Chinese verbs often need a complement showing the result, direction or possibility of the action; it must fit the verb and the meaning.
en.hint: What is the result or direction of the action in “{l}”? Which word right after the verb shows that?

en.label: 把 / 被 construction
en.meta: 把 puts a definite object before the verb when something is done to it; 被 marks the passive. The verb then needs a result or other element after it.
en.hint: In “{l}”, who does what to what? Where must the object go, and what must follow the verb?

en.label: Separable verb
en.meta: Verb-object compounds (见面, 帮忙, 睡觉) split: 了, durations and extra objects go inside the compound or need a coverb, not after the whole word.
en.hint: The verb in “{l}” is really verb + object. Where can 了, a duration or another person go?

en.label: Coverb
en.meta: Coverbs (在, 给, 跟, 对, 从…) introduce a place, recipient or partner and normally stand before the main verb; each verb selects its own.
en.hint: Which coverb introduces the person or place in “{l}”, and does that phrase go before or after the verb?

en.label: Connective
en.meta: Chinese connectives often come in fixed pairs (因为…所以, 虽然…但是, 不但…而且) and have fixed positions relative to the subject.
en.hint: What relationship links the clauses in “{l}”? What is the matching partner of the connective?

en.label: Topic–comment structure
en.meta: This language often states the topic first and then comments on it; building the sentence subject-first as in English sounds unnatural here.
en.hint: What is “{l}” really about? Try putting that topic first and then saying something about it.

en.label: は / が
en.meta: が marks the subject inside a noun-modifying or subordinate clause and question-word subjects; は marks the topic of the whole sentence.
en.hint: Is the noun before the particle in “{l}” the topic of the whole sentence, or the subject inside a smaller clause?

en.label: Case particle
en.meta: Case particles (を, に, で, へ, と, から…) show each noun's role; the verb decides which particle its nouns take.
en.hint: What role does the noun in “{l}” play for its verb — object, place of action, destination, tool? Which particle marks that role?

en.label: Particle
en.meta: Particles such as も, だけ, しか, まで, や add meanings like 'also', 'only', 'as far as' or 'and so on'; each has its own nuance.
en.hint: What nuance does the original need at “{l}” — also, only, a limit, a list of examples? Which particle carries it?

en.label: Conjugation
en.meta: The stem is right but the ending is built incorrectly for its conjugation class (godan, ichidan, irregular; い- or な-adjective).
en.hint: Which conjugation group does the verb or adjective in “{l}” belong to? How does that group build this form?

en.label: Tense / aspect
en.meta: Endings like 〜る, 〜た, 〜ている, 〜ていた must match when the action happens and whether it is ongoing, completed or a resulting state.
en.hint: Is the action in “{l}” finished, ongoing, habitual or still to come? Which ending expresses that?

en.label: Politeness level
en.meta: Politeness level (plain, です/ます, honorific, humble) must stay consistent with the passage and suit who is addressed or discussed.
en.hint: What politeness level do the other sentences use? Does the ending of “{l}” match it?

en.label: Counter
en.meta: Japanese counts with counters chosen by the kind of object (〜つ, 〜個, 〜本, 〜枚, 〜人…); number + counter readings can change.
en.hint: What kind of object is being counted in “{l}”? Which counter fits it?

en.label: Transitive / intransitive, voice
en.meta: Japanese has transitive/intransitive verb pairs (開ける/開く) plus passive, causative and potential forms; the form must match who acts and the particles used.
en.hint: In “{l}”, does someone do the action to something, or does it happen by itself? Which verb of the pair (or which voice) fits?

en.label: Noun modification
en.meta: Modifiers precede the noun in a set form: verbs in plain form, い-adjectives as they are, な-adjectives with な, nouns with の.
en.hint: How should the describing part in “{l}” connect to its noun — plain form, な, or の?

en.label: Clause linking
en.meta: Clauses are joined with 〜て, 〜たり, 〜と, 〜ば, 〜たら, 〜ので, 〜のに…; each expresses a different relationship and has its own restrictions.
en.hint: How are the two actions around “{l}” related — sequence, condition, reason, examples? Which linking form expresses that?

en.label: Kanji choice
en.meta: Words with the same reading can be written with different kanji carrying different meanings; pick the kanji that fits this meaning.
en.hint: The reading in “{l}” is right — which kanji with that reading has the meaning needed here?
